text: CoinDCX Faces Suspected $16 Million Hack After $44 Million Breach in 2025 India's CoinDCX, one of the country's largest cryptocurrency exchanges, may have suffered another security breach, according to on-chain investigator Darcy. On October 21, approximately 15.99 million USDT and 5,784 TRX were transferred from CoinDCX hot wallets and deposit addresses to a single TRON address, including one transfer of 15.82 million USDT. The funds were subsequently split and routed to deposit addresses at Binance, OKX and Gate. CoinDCX previously lost about $44 million in a July 2025 hack. The latest suspected theft has not been officially confirmed. In response to reports of suspicious outflows, CoinDCX and co-founder Sumit Gupta issued statements assuring users that funds remain safe, asserting that flagged transactions originated from legacy addresses compromised during its July 2025 exploit and abandoned since. Gupta maintained that no active CoinDCX hot wallets were breached and characterized the movement as hackers reusing obsolete addresses. Blockchain investigator ZachXBT swiftly disputed CoinDCX's explanation, providing on-chain evidence showing that the flagged deposit address remained active with a liquidity provider for ten months post-hack, routinely sweeping user deposits and interacting with CoinDCX's current hot wallet as recently as April and May 2026, indicating that roughly $15.8 million in user deposits was unaccounted for by the exchange. CoinDCX has not yet provided further comment. CoinDCX released an updated statement regarding the on-chain activity on the flagged wallets, including the TQKJQ address, stating that the addresses in question were legacy addresses deprecated after being compromised in the July 2025 exploit, and that operational losses occurred due to user deposit errors combined with a failure in the platform's automated sweeping process. The exchange noted that it absorbed these losses in full and that affected users who deposited to deprecated addresses have been duly credited. Additionally, CoinDCX stated that customer assets remain secure in segregated cold storage, and that current active hot wallets and user funds have not been impacted. ZachXBT urged users to withdraw their funds from CoinDCX as soon as possible, severely criticizing its co-founders as either lying or grossly incompetent. He stated that the platform initially denied any theft both publicly and privately, only to later disclose a $16 million asset theft, which failed to maintain transparency with the public from the start and wasted the industry's time. — link

text: INTEL: China moves to seize 61,800 BTC tied to a $5.7B fraud Chinese prosecutors asked a Tianjin court to confiscate the coins as illegal gains. The court accepted the request on Oct 13 and opened a six-month window for victims and other parties to join the case. The coins trace to Qian Zhimin's alleged scheme, which raised over 40B yuan from 102,000+ investors between 2014 and 2017. Qian fled to the UK in 2017 and British authorities seized the bitcoin. Days ago a UK High Court ruled that Chinese law governs victims' claims to the coins. CoinDesk says that boosts the British government's chances of keeping them. Some victims' lawyers are seeking to appeal. Full story Twitter | News
